claims.value: Seen to emerge almost vertically from cloud and crashed near Oswestry; witnesses said it clipped trees and a high-tension wire, then burned
claims.quote: Seen to emerge almost vertically from cloud & crashed near Oswestry.

claims.value: 4 metres up on the tree trunk, A495, Llynclys, Oswestry, Shropshire, SY10 8LU

IN HONOUR OF/ WHO BRAVELY FOUGHT TO LAND BURNING &/ BADLY DAMAGED HAMPDEN BOMBER No P1294/ WITHOUT INJURY TO OTHERS./ THIS TREE ADDING ANOTHER OBSTACLE TO/ THE FATAL CRASH IN FIELD OPPOSITE/ KILLING ALL CREW./ OCTOBER 30TH 1941
The Hampden crashed in a field at White Lion crossroads on Llynclys Hill, near Oswestry
The crash happened at about 14:30 in the afternoon
The aircraft had just cleared the Berwyn mountains in very poor visibility and driving rain, and the pilot had just been given a corrected course back to Cottesmore
Witnesses said the aircraft came out of cloud and dived almost vertically; other reports say it had levelled out, as if attempting an emergency landing
The aircraft caught fire at once and exploded shortly after the crash; all four crew died

The plaque's inscription says the crew fought to land the burning, damaged bomber without injury to others, that the tree added another obstacle to the fatal crash in the field opposite, and that all crew were killed

IBCC describes the Llynclys memorial as a stencilled wooden board beside the A495 and transcribes it as 'In honour of the crew of Hampden P1294 October 30th 1941'; IWM describes a black board with gilt lettering and shows a '(Names)' placeholder after 'IN HONOUR OF'
IBCC lists a stone tablet in the Church of St. Nicholas, Cottesmore, for the British and American personnel stationed at the station who died in 1939-1945
The Aircrew Remembered page gives no formal inquiry or board finding for the loss
Sgt Williams had a brother who also died on service; Aircrew Remembered gives him as LAC Stanly Rhys Williams, killed on 5 March 1943 while training as a navigator in South Africa
Sgt Tatton's brother Sgt Cyril Tatton was listed missing, believed killed, on a daylight operation to Brest on 24 July 1941 and is on the Runnymede Memorial
Brompton Cemetery, Northallerton, Sec. C, Grave 111

paragraphs.text: Hampden I P1294 of 14 Operational Training Unit took off from RAF Cottesmore on a cross-country navigation flight and crashed at about 14:30 on 30 October 1941 in a field at White Lion crossroads on Llynclys Hill, near Oswestry. Aircrew Remembered says the aircraft had just cleared the Berwyn mountains in very poor visibility and driving rain, and that the pilot had just been given a corrected course back to Cottesmore. IBCC records it as seen to emerge almost vertically from cloud. Aircrew Remembered adds that witnesses saw it clip trees and a high-tension wire before it crashed, caught fire and exploded; other reports say it had levelled out, as if trying to land. All four crew died. We found no formal inquiry finding.

The pilot was Flying Officer George Donald Kerr (26), son of Richard and Isabella Kerr and husband of Phyllis, buried at Liverpool (Allerton) Cemetery. The observer was Sergeant Ivor Morgan Williams (19) of Newport, buried at Cardiff (Cathays) Cemetery; his brother also died on service. The two wireless operator/air gunners were Sergeant Douglas Tatton (21) of Erdington, Birmingham, buried at Erdington (St Barnabas) Churchyard, and Sergeant Herbert Playforth (21) of York, buried at Brompton Cemetery, Northallerton. Tatton had lost his brother Cyril on a Brest raid three months earlier. All four served in the RAFVR. Tatton's details rest on Aircrew Remembered alone.

IWM records a black wooden board with gilt lettering, about 450mm square, fixed 4 metres up a tree trunk beside the A495 at Llynclys, in good condition. Its inscription honours those who fought to land the burning, damaged bomber without injury to others, that the tree added another obstacle to the fatal crash in the field opposite, and that all crew were killed. IWM does not transcribe whatever follows 'IN HONOUR OF'. IBCC transcribes the board as 'In honour of the crew of Hampden P1294' and calls it stencilled. IBCC also lists a tablet for Cottesmore station personnel in the Church of St. Nicholas, Cottesmore. IWM does not state who made or erected the board, when, or who looks after it.

notes: NO IWM CAPTURE: research/iwm/ holds no file for this memorial; the live IWM page was read instead. WHO THE PLAQUE HONOURS: the IWM inscription shows a '(Names)' placeholder after 'IN HONOUR OF', so IWM names nobody. IBCC (Williams record) transcribes the board as 'In honour of the crew of Hampden P1294 October 30th 1941', so the gap is probably a crew reference, not F/O Kerr. We cannot say which reading the physical board carries; a site visit or photo would settle it. The inscription claim keeps the existing record text unchanged. PHOTOS: IWM has three photos by Tony Hibberd (sh_llynclys_1-3.jpg) but the full media URLs were not read, so none are included. TATTON: no CWGC or IBCC page found; rank, role, age, number, burial, parents and brother come from Aircrew Remembered only, so single source. Role/age/number for Williams and Playforth, and burial for all three others, are corroborated by CWGC or IBCC. Kerr's number is 87062 per CWGC and IBCC; search snippets of RAFCommands (not read in full) show 87026 on one page, treated as a typo. A RAFCommands forum snippet placed Kerr at Glasgow (Riddrie Park); CWGC says Allerton, not used. MINOR DISCREPANCIES: IBCC gives Kerr's group as 5 Group and Williams's as 7 Group (14 OTU was 7 Group per IBCC Williams and Playforth); not recorded. IBCC says day sortie, Aircrew Remembered gives 14:30; consistent. Aviation Safety Network (wikibase 193344) returned 403 and was not read; its search snippet gives the serial as R1294 in the narrative and P1294 in the registration field. WILLIAMS'S BROTHER: Aircrew Remembered spells the name Stanly, IBCC Stanley; not asserted in the narrative beyond 'his brother'. Aircrew Remembered credits Kelvin Youngs/KTY (2016) and quotes Chorley's Bomber Command Losses as a source, so its Cottesmore facts are not independent of Chorley. CUSTODIAN: IWM states none; no other source names one; status 'unknown' not 'unknown-confirmed' as the parish council and local history groups were not searched. Page footer shows Aircrew Remembered modified 02 Nov 2026. Leads: Llynclys/Whittington parish council, Oswestry local history groups, Shropshire History site (credited by Aircrew Remembered). The Cottesmore tablet is a station memorial, not specific to this crew.
